 Knicks Sign Dalton Knecht, Waive Kevin McCullar Jr.
 By Arthur Hill |
 at October 23, 2026 6:18 pm 
 6:18 pm:  Knecht’s two-way contract is now official, according to the Knicks ( Twitter links ), who confirmed that McCullar has been placed on waivers.
 10:25 am: Former Laker Dalton Knecht will join the Knicks on a two-way contract, his agents at Excel Sports tell ESPN’s Shams Charania ( Twitter link ). New York will waive Kevin McCullar Jr. to create a two-way opening, according to Michael Scotto of HoopsHype ( Twitter link ).
 The Knicks were among several teams that expressed interest in Knecht, who was waived by L.A. over the weekend to trim its roster down to 15 players. The Kings, Timberwolves and Raptors were also mentioned as teams that might be willing to offer a two-way deal.
 The 25-year-old small forward was viewed as a potential rotation piece when the Lakers selected him out of Tennessee with the 17th pick in the 2024 draft. However, he wasn’t able to provide the scoring production that was expected and he was facing a diminished role in L.A. even if he had made the team.
 After appearing in 78 games as a rookie, Knecht saw his playing time cut nearly in half to 10.2 minutes per night in 54 games last season. He averaged 4.2 points and 1.2 rebounds while shooting 45.5% from the field and 34.2% from three-point range.
 Knecht may see time with the Knicks’ G League affiliate in Westchester as he adjusts to a new organization. He will be eligible to play up to 49 NBA games this season as long as he remains on a two-way contract.
 New York is technically the second NBA team for Knecht, but he was briefly traded to Charlotte at the 2025 deadline as part of the return for Mark Williams . That deal was rescinded when Williams failed his physical, and Knecht was returned to the Lakers without ever playing for the Hornets.
 McCullar, a 25-year-old small forward, was in his third straight year with the Knicks on a two-way contract. He appeared in 21 NBA games last season. averaging 2.4 points, 1.3 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 7.4 minutes per night. He did earn a championship ring and got to take part in Tuesday’s ring night ceremony, Scotto notes.

 Joking aside, I knew this was coming because teams rarely carry Two-Ways at overlapping positions. These guys are injury replacements / organizational depth. The only time we really see it is if there are extreme injury issues (i.e. long-term injury to a starter).
 In this case one of these SGs has a significantly higher pedigree & performance than the other.
 Dalton Knecht (17th pick in 2024)
Age 25 / 2,047 career minutes
60 2PT%, 37 3PT%, 76 FT% (57 TS%, 18 USG%)
 Kevin McCullar (56th pick in 2024)
Age 25 / 184 career minutes
48 2PT%, 32 3PT%, 57 FT% (49 TS%, 16 USG%)
 All these Knicks fans who tell you they liked K-Mac are only looking at him on one side of the ball. He was a decidedly negative offensive player and he’s already near the top of his development curve. Maybe he gets a better chance in another organization that isn’t a contender with an NBA ironman and a top 10 wing.
 Knecht as much as he’s “disappointed”, has played 10x as many NBA minutes. Say what you will about him as a player, his defense is not as damaging as McCullar’s offense, especially at the SG position. Landry Shamet wasn’t the world’s greatest defender either. Neither were AJ Green or Sam Merrill, these guys have all figured out how to defend. McCullar is never going to shoot like that, and he’s never going to finish like Knecht either.
